text: Coccidiosis affects piglets from about 1 to 3 weeks old, causing yellow-to-grey (rarely bloody) diarrhea of creamy to doughy consistency. Piglets rarely die but become thin, rough-coated, and inactive, reaching weaning in poor commercial condition. Treatment with Sulfadimidine (Sulfa 33, Septotryl) gives mixed results — prevention matters much more: a single Toltrazuril dose (Baycox, Anticoc) 3 days after birth. Hygiene measures that reduce coccidia levels in the pen: clean out feces and creep feed from the floor, renovate wet/poor floor surfaces, control fly populations, use disposable nesting material (remembering that coccidia eggs/oocysts resist disinfectants), and wash and sun-dry any reusable bedding.
